verdicts.tldr: caller.Func != nil is always true, so the conjunct guards a state the accessor already rules out
verdicts.details: peekCallFrame returns a frame only from inside `if fr.IsCall()` (machine.go:2919-2921), and IsCall is `return fr.Func != nil` (frame.go:78-80). So `caller != nil && caller.Func != nil` is exactly `caller != nil`, and the second conjunct is a branch no input reaches. TestHarnessSeedsCur's three subtests cover caller==nil, a testing caller and a realm caller; none can reach Func==nil, so the reader who wonders when it fires has to re-derive the accessor's invariant. Fix: drop `&& caller.Func != nil`.
verdicts.evidence: read only, no mutation: frame.go:78-80 `func (fr *Frame) IsCall() bool { return fr.Func != nil }`; machine.go:2919-2921 `fr := &m.Frames[i]; if fr.IsCall() { if n == 1 { return fr }`; op_call.go:559-561 `caller := m.PeekCallFrame(2)` then `return caller != nil && caller.Func != nil && caller.Func.PkgPath == TestingBasePkgPath`. harnessSeedsCur is absent from the base worktree's op_call.go.
verdicts.verify_by: read frame.go:78-80 and machine.go:2915-2930; drop `&& caller.Func != nil` and run `go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run TestHarnessSeedsCur`

verdicts.tldr: the fixture's only written assertion cannot fire, so the stdlib suite ships an example of a check the project documents as always true
verdicts.details: curSubtestTarget is crossing (first param `cur realm`), so its own frame Cur is installed from the value passed and that frame is then the topmost crossing frame; realmIsCurrentOnMachine compares the value's HIV to exactly that frame's Cur HIV (uverse.go:613-615), so `cur.IsCurrent()` is true by construction and the panic arm is dead. The tree says so itself: interrealm_v2.md:338-339 reads `Crossing functions do not require cur.IsCurrent() because the runtime ensures that it is always true`. What survives is the fixture's real assertion, that the t.Run dispatch does not panic, which fires at the closure's entry on line 18 before curSubtestTarget is called at all, so the 25-line file keeps its full regression power at 22 lines without the guard. Fix: drop the guard and let the sub-test body be the call, or assert something the dispatch does not already guarantee.
verdicts.evidence: read only: uverse.go:613-615 `topHIV := topmostCrossingFrameCurHIV(m); return topHIV != nil && topHIV == checkHIV`; adr/interrealm_v2.md:338-339 quoted above; cur_subtest_test.gno:11-20, target at 11-15, literal at 18. 25 lines at head, 22 in the finder's rewrite; the rewrite's green (`ok github.com/gnolang/gno/gnovm/pkg/gnolang 2.889s`) and the exemption-removed FAIL are the finder's runs, not rerun here as this batch is read-only. verdicts.tldr: Crossing: true on the callee fixture is never read, so the test overstates what the exemption is conditioned on
verdicts.details: harnessSeedsCur reads only `caller.Func.PkgPath` (op_call.go:559-561), and PeekCallFrame(2) selects frames by `fr.IsCall()`, that is `Func != nil` (frame.go:78-80), so the callee fixture needs a non-nil Func and nothing more. All three subtests build the callee as `Frame{Func: &FuncValue{Crossing: true}}`, which reads as if the exemption depended on the callee being crossing; deleting the field changes no assertion. The real condition on the callee lives in installInheritedCur's `if fv.IsCrossing() && fv.nativeBody == nil && fr.Cur.T == nil && len(b.Values) > curIdx` (op_call.go:443), which this unit test never enters. Fix: drop `Crossing: true` from the three fixtures, or add one line saying the field is there only to make the frame a call frame.
verdicts.evidence: read only: op_call.go:559-561 harnessSeedsCur body; frame.go:78-80; op_call_test.go:85-105, the three `Frame{Func: &FuncValue{Crossing: true}}` callee frames. TestHarnessSeedsCur is added by this diff (hunk op_call_test.go @@ -59,40 +59,78 @@).
verdicts.verify_by: read op_call.go:558-561, then delete 'Crossing: true' from the three fixtures and run go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestHarnessSeedsCur'

verdicts.tldr: the leading int parameter is what keeps two helpers non-crossing, and deleting it as filler breaks the fixture at preprocess
verdicts.details: FuncType.IsCrossing tests the first parameter alone, `fpt := ft.Params[0].Type; return fpt == gRealmType` (types.go:1393-1399), so `func rangeLocal(r realm)` and `func setPkgCur(r realm)` would both become crossing, and preprocess.go:2827 then panics with `a crossing function's first realm argument must have name "cur"` at the declaration. The file's header comment explains the three binding shapes and says nothing about the parameter that makes two of them legal. Two limits on the finding: namedResult's `x int` is not load-bearing, since a zero-parameter function is non-crossing by the same accessor, and interrealm_v2.md:330-334 already documents `_ int, rlm realm` as the common pattern after the v2 refactor, so the idiom is explained in the tree, just not in this file. Fix: one clause on the header comment saying the leading int keeps the realm parameter out of first position.
verdicts.evidence: read only: types.go:1393-1399; preprocess.go:2824-2829 `if pn != "cur" && !strings.HasPrefix(string(pn), ".arg") { panic(...) }`; zrealm_cur_other_legal.gno:11, 16, 21. File absent at the merge base.
verdicts.verify_by: delete `x int` from rangeLocal and run `go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_cur_other_legal.gno$'`: the file goes red.

verdicts.tldr: the ADR merges under a literal xxxx placeholder with a Status naming a branch that gets deleted, so the record cannot be mapped back to the change
verdicts.details: The file ships as `prxxxx_cur_binding_followups.md` and its Status reads `Implemented on fix/cur-binding-followups. PR number pending.`; after merge the branch is gone and the number is known, so the permanent record keeps a placeholder for both. Two of the finder's supporting premises are wrong and must be dropped before this is posted: `ls gnovm/adr` shows six other entries naming neither a PR nor a sha (interrealm_v2.md, migration_guide.md, native_input_bounds.md, op_handler_gas_audit.md, pr_bigdec_rat.md, pr_cross_explicit.md, plus the STORAGE_* files), so it is not the only one, and `grep -rn 'prxxxx' gnovm/` returns zero content hits, not three, since the placeholder is in the filename alone. What is left is a one-line rename and a Status edit at merge time. Fix: rename to pr6196_cur_binding_followups.md and set Status to the merged PR.
verdicts.evidence: read only: `ls gnovm/adr` (47 entries, listed above); `sed -n '1,14p' gnovm/adr/prxxxx_cur_binding_followups.md` gives `## Status` then `Implemented on \`fix/cur-binding-followups\`. PR number pending.`; `grep -rn 'prxxxx' gnovm/` returns no lines. File absent at the merge base.
verdicts.verify_by: ls gnovm/adr and compare every entry's naming with the new file; grep -rn 'prxxxx' gnovm/ returns 3 hits, all added by this PR

verdicts.tldr: the deferred gas-metering gap is tracked in a repository the comment's own readers may not be able to open, unverified here
verdicts.details: The counts hold: `grep the head worktree for the NOTE's cross-repo issue reference` returns exactly three lines, all added by this PR (op_call.go:452 and adr lines 69 and 106), and the one comparable cross-reference in the package points at the same repository's tracker, nocompile_on_32bits.go:7 `Please see https://github.com/gnolang/gno/issues/3288`. Whether a gnolang/gno contributor can actually open a tracker outside this repository is the whole finding and no check here settles it: this batch is read-only and made no network call. Calibration also puts a finding about a code comment's own wording at SKIP whatever its band, so it stays out of the inline slots either way. Fix: confirm the tracker's visibility, and if it is not public, add a gnolang/gno issue for the unmetered install walk and name it beside the existing reference.
verdicts.evidence: read only: the two greps above, run in the head worktree; the NOTE at op_call.go:445-452 ends `so it is deferred to ride with the other gas schedule work instead of this fix, see a tracker outside this repository`. No 'that tracker' hit anywhere in the base worktree's op_call.go. What would confirm it: opening a tracker outside this repository as an unaffiliated account, or the repository's visibility field.
